rē^-trūdo , no
I.perf., sum, 3, v. a., to thrust back (in the verb. finit. only anteand post-class.): “quasi retruderet hominum me vis invitum,” Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 64 : “in metallum retrudendus, Cod. Th. 1, 5, 1: in carcerem,” Vulg. Gen. 41, 10 . — Hence, rē^-trūsus , a, um, P. a., removed, concealed; several times in Cic. with abditus: “simulacra deorum,” Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 3, § 7 .—Trop.: “voluntas,” Q. Cic. Petit. Cons. 11, 44 : “haec in philosophiā,” Cic. de Or. 1, 19, 87 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
